legal_currentness_checks.jurisdiction: United States federal copyright, selected statutory propositions only

verified_propositions.proposition: The book distinguishes the musical composition from the fixed sound recording; current Title 17 lists both as distinct categories and gives sound recordings a separately limited rights scope.
The current statute protects original works fixed in a tangible medium, lists musical works and sound recordings, and excludes ideas and systems from protection.

The source distinguishes copyright protection/initial ownership from registration; current §§ 201 and 408 place initial ownership with author(s) and state that registration is not a condition of protection.

The book discusses authorship and intent as separate joint-work issues; current § 101 defines a joint work through authorship and intent that contributions be merged, while § 201 makes joint-work authors coowners.

The source describes employee/scope and qualifying commissioned work as separate routes. Current § 101 and Circular 30 confirm employee work within scope or a statutorily listed commissioned category with express signed writing.
The book describes transfers and licenses as different arrangements; current § 204 requires a signed writing for a transfer of copyright ownership other than by operation of law.

Current § 106 enumerates reproduction, derivative-work, distribution, public-performance and display rights, with a distinct digital-audio-transmission right for sound recordings, subject to statutory limitations.
Current §§ 408, 411 and 412 separately address permissive registration, civil-action prerequisites for U.S. works, and timing limits on certain remedies.
The source discusses fair use factor analysis and case-specific outcomes; current § 107 identifies four nonexclusive factors and illustrative purposes.

The source distinguishes composition mechanical licensing from a master-use license; current § 115 provides conditional routes for reproduction/distribution of nondramatic musical works, including the statutory digital blanket pathway for covered activities.
